note: over-long hex with an L suffix passed the suffix to createBigInteger, which rejects it; fix strips it under an isLongCh ternary keeping the original str as else-branch, so preserved

setNullString built quotedNullString from the raw, possibly null quoteCharacter instead of the defaulted quote setQuote used, giving null text around the marker; the line is rewritten into a shared helper, not guarded

accumulators for seconds to years were declared int and could overflow when a long period is folded into smaller units; fix declares them long like milliseconds, a type substitution in six declarations
a string ending on a separator produced an extra empty trailing token; fix adds a guard adding it only if non-empty or all tokens are preserved, addition only

sub-hour fields were removed with Calendar.set(), which resolves an ambiguous DST-overlap wall time to standard time and shifts the result an hour; fix adds arithmetic cases, original set() kept as default branch
event counter increment could overflow and wrap negative; fix adds a saturation guard, the ternary re-wrapped as an if and the original sum kept verbatim as the guard's else-branch
wrong method at both comment line ends: println() also writes the records' trailing delimiter; fix substitutes a new helper writing only the record separator, the call replaced rather than guarded
rejection cap max(64, gap * 10) was too small for ranges with few acceptable values, so valid requests could throw; fix uses 64 << gapBits in long, a wrong bound value

WildcardTypeImpl reported no upper bound instead of the implicit Object and hashed with its own formula, breaking equals and hashCode with equal JDK wildcards; fix changes the default and replaces the hash algorithm
BC dates give negative week years that the digit rules cannot render; fix adds a sign guard in the int overload and routes the calendar overload through it, original delegate call kept verbatim
array max and min used > and < with an explicit NaN check, treating -0.0 and 0.0 as equal unlike Math.max and Math.min; fix replaces that approach with them in four overloads
ceiling always rounded up, even when the date already sat on the boundary and truncation changed nothing; the existing CEILING condition gains a clause comparing against the original millis

addSub overflow-checked each int cross product, rejecting sums whose result fits an int; fix computes in long and narrows only the final numerator, rewriting the overflow approach; now-unused helpers deleted

isDelimiter consumes a multi-character delimiter's trailing characters but was evaluated twice for the same character, in the whitespace loop and the test after it; fix remembers the first result, a reader-state fault
padded text was passed to Formatter.format as the format string, so a percent sign in it was parsed as a specifier; fix passes it as an argument under SIMPLEST_FORMAT, an API misuse
Integer.parseInt accepts a leading sign, so a unicode escape with + or - among its four hex digits was decoded; fix adds a sign check throwing IllegalArgumentException, addition only

print synchronized on the CSVFormat instance instead of the existing writeLock, so it was not mutually exclusive with code locking writeLock; fix moves the body into a writeLock block, a concurrency fault

static invocation could resolve an instance method of matching signature and invoke it on null; the candidate null check and the search filter gain an is-static clause, same check in both invoke paths

era names came from DateFormatSymbols.getEras(), which knows only Gregorian eras, even for non-Gregorian calendars, giving wrong names or AIOOBE; fix adds a calendar-aware era rule replacing the TextField call, an API misuse
hex strings for Integer.MIN_VALUE and Long.MIN_VALUE were promoted to a wider type, the extra negative magnitude ignored; both existing size conditions gain a !isNegativeMinimum clause

append(Object) guarded its own recursion with the shared reflection REGISTRY, so an object whose hashCode used reflection was skipped as a cycle; fix gives append a separate registry, an identity fault

month-only patterns used format-context month names where SimpleDateFormat on Java 9+ uses standalone ones, wrong in Slavic languages; fix guards with ternaries keeping the original arrays as else-branch; L-case hoisting is refactoring
the L-suffix branch accepted only a leading minus sign, so +123L was rejected; the existing sign test gains the plus alternative through isSign, a missing clause

with ignoreCase the search string was lowercased by String.toLowerCase(), locale-sensitive and able to change its length, though the search is already case-insensitive; fix removes the call, an API misuse

the class-loader-aware stream resolved classes through its loader but left proxies to the default name-based lookup; fix records proxy classes while serialising and reuses them, rewriting clone's serialisation rather than adding to it

the reused escapeDelimiterBuf kept characters from an earlier peek when a later peek read fewer, so stale data could match the escaped delimiter; fix clears it first, a stale-state initialisation fault
an escaped field equal to the null string after unescaping was still read as null; the existing quoted-field exception gains an isEscaped clause, backed by a new token flag

multiplyBy cancelled only cross terms, so a factor shared within an unreduced operand survived into the product and overflowed; fix reduces both operands first and rewires the gcd and product lines to them
split() set stopTimeNanos but not stopInstant, leaving the stop instant stale after a split; same missing refresh in both overloads, a derived field not refreshed, so STATE
DATE parsed Date.toString() output with the default locale, failing where month and day names are not English; fix keeps the original parse in a try and falls back to Locale.ENGLISH in the catch
arrayMemberHash had no branch for annotation arrays, which fell through to the generic array hash, inconsistent with the annotation-aware equals; fix adds the branch and a helper, addition only
read() added the encoded length of EOF to bytesRead; the existing encoder != null condition gains a current != EOF clause
